judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble leaves the execution date blank ("as of June __, 2004"), a visible mechanical gap that could matter for when obligations began. Otherwise the parties are identified with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Schedule A and Section 2.1(ii)'s admission of LSB and DMSA as Members; no conflict found elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital garbles the statute's name ("the Maine Lunited Liability Company" with 'Act' omitted), a mechanical error in the very definition it purports to create. The defined term "Maine Act" is nonetheless separately and correctly defined in Article I.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital's stated intent to form under Maine law tracks Sections 2.1 and 17.9, though the company's only real operations sit in Holyoke, Massachusetts under Section 2.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration recital with settled meaning; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the capital contribution provisions of Article IV and Schedule A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional definitions preface; the "unless the context otherwise requires" carve-out is boilerplate rather than a genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs Article I generally and does not contradict any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition with no operative content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 does in fact define Additional Members, so the reference is sound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Control" is defined by the elastic phrase "power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies ... by contract or otherwise," a boundary that is hard to apply but is the market-standard formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Section 12.7's grant to "DMSA or an Affiliate thereof," which is where any real fight over its reach would arise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential and definite; no term carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.10's amendment mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition tied to a public filing; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 requires that a copy of "the Certificate" be kept — a term never defined, presumably meaning the Articles, a mismatch between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition with no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VI throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cross-reference definition; the only oddity is an OCR typo ("tn").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 does establish Capital Accounts, and Section 15.3(ii) distributes by Capital Account balance, so the term does real work consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: money plus fair market value of property contributed under Section 4.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A's figure for LSB ($00,001.00) is garbled, which makes the "agreed value" this definition depends on uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard tax-code definition with an express successor-provision rule; no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Articles VIII and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific entity; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8 instead speaks of consent "of the LLC," an undefined variant of this term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sprawling enumeration (Members, Directors, Officers, Managers, their Affiliates, and those Affiliates' officers, employees, agents) whose outer boundary is genuinely hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.11 confers rights on no one "except the Members and Managers," which sits awkwardly with indemnity rights given to all Covered Persons under Section 12.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but harmless one-line definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1 and 6.6 (Removal).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause numbering is garbled ("(11)" for (ii)) and clause (iii) then refers back to "Clause (ii)," a mechanical wrinkle that is nonetheless resolvable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Article VIII allocations and Section 9.1 without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such Member's interest of the profits and losses" is ungrammatical (for "in"), and the term conflates voting rights with economic rights in one bundle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XVI treats "Interests" as divisible into voting and economic components while this definition bundles them, and Section 16.6 refers to "LLC Votes" rather than Member Votes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) sweeps in "all policies, practices and guidelines of any governmental body" — a general catch-all appended to hard-edged legal instruments, and the numbering repeats "(i)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Law" is used in Sections 2.2, 6.6 and 9.3 without obvious strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise statutory citation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout; only Section 6.1's stray reference to "the Act" departs from it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its face: a majority of Member Votes, by writing or vote.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the separately defined "Majority" immediately following, and Section 5.5 uses both terms for different functions (quorum versus decision).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Majority" defined as "a majority of the Member Votes" is a quantity, yet Section 5.5(vii) speaks of "A Majority present in person or by proxy," treating it as persons.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The near-identity with "Majority Vote" (c020) leaves it unclear whether the two terms are meant to differ where both appear in Section 5.5(vii)-(viii) and 5.5(xi).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, with an express inclusion of Directors.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 says election as Director designates a Manager, which is consistent; Section 17.11's "Managers" carve-out then sweeps in Directors.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "'Members' means two (2) or more of such Persons" is an odd numerical floor that would break the plural usages if the Company ever had one member.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) contemplates a Member ceasing membership with "all of the remaining Members" continuing, which with two members is hard to square with this floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines votes solely by reference to a schedule "as may be amended," leaving the substantive entitlement outside the definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary update Schedule A without that being an amendment, while Section 17.10 requires unanimity to amend — a real tension over who can change voting power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reserve carve-out ("any amounts determined by the Members to be necessary to provide a reasonable reserve for working-capital needs or any other contingencies") is an open-ended discretion that can swallow the distribution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the cash receipts and disbursements method while Section 10.2 mandates accrual accounting, and it gives the reserve decision to the Members while Section 9.2 gives distributions to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line circular definition; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes the interest by Schedule A yet adds "as determined by the unanimous written consent of the Members as adjusted from time to time," leaving two possible controlling sources.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) has the Secretary unilaterally update Schedule A and says such revisions are not amendments, which cuts against the unanimity this definition requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list uses the capitalised defined term "Company" where "corporation" was plainly intended, a mechanical error that makes the definition partly circular, and it ends with an "other legal entity" catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Company" is separately defined as Dialogo, LLC, so this usage is at war with c013 wherever "Person" is applied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Profits and Losses simply as taxable income or loss under a mis-typed "§ 703{a)", with none of the usual book-value adjustments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(iv) says the allocations are intended to comply with § 704(b) and the Treasury Regulations, which normally require book (not purely tax) Profits — a fit problem with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Board appoints, and duties are cross-referenced to Section 7.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.1(iii) and 2.6 impose further Secretary duties not mentioned in 7.4, but they are additive rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1 supplies the meaning as promised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard and precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4(ii) refers to "Regulation section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)" rather than the defined term, a trivial slip.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional headings clause; its own meaning is not in doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It usefully neutralises the duplicated "Section 6.6" headings but does not cure the numbering error itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly mechanical formation language; the statement that Schedule A revisions "shall not be deemed an amendment" is clear in wording though strong in effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lets the Secretary alter Schedule A — the very document that fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes — free of Section 17.10's unanimous amendment requirement and of the Percentage Interest definition's unanimity condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain and administrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6's fictitious-name registrations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Continue in perpetuity, unless ... dissolved" is definite, with a separate rule for legal existence until cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XV's dissolution events are expressly preserved by the "unless" clause, so the two harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific agent and office; the residual power to change is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It vests the change in "the Members" while Section 2.5 gives the parallel power over the principal office to the Board, an inconsistency of allocation though a minor one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific address and a clear power to relocate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.1(i) routes all notices to the Company to this address, so a Board relocation could displace the notice provision without amendment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mandate covers jurisdictions where the Company "transacts business" but the Secretary's filing duty covers those where it "may wish to conduct business" — two different triggers in one section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 2.2 and the Secretary's role under Section 7.4 without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Developing Spanish language newspaper(s) and media" is a vague statement of scope, and it is then swallowed by "any lawful act or activity" — a specific purpose against an unlimited catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 restrains LSB from services "to the extent it relates to the business," so the reach of this purpose clause directly controls the scope of the exclusivity covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long "including, but not limited to" enumeration of corporate powers; boilerplate, though the catch-all against thirteen specifics invites ejusdem generis argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several enumerated powers (borrowing at (k), contracts with Members at (b), disposing of assets at (d)) are subjected to unanimous Board approval by Section 6.8, which is expressly "notwithstanding any other provision."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: merger requires approval of all Members.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8 requires unanimous Board approval for asset dispositions and equity issuances but says nothing about mergers, leaving the two approval regimes side by side rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Has contributed or is deemed to have contributed" leaves open whether any cash actually moved, and the operative amounts live entirely off-page in Schedule A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A's LSB figure is garbled ($00,001.00 against a 49% interest), and Section 6.8(iii) singles out reimbursement of DMSA's "initial capital contributions" — so what was contributed is contested ground across provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, settled propositions of LLC law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's partition waiver and Section 15.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii)(a) is mangled — "the respective invoices of each of DMSA" (a plural construction with one named party, apparently dropping LSB) and "as it receives payment form such customer" — and (b) uses "Membership Interests," a term the Agreement never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The DMSA invoice exception cuts against Section 9.1's pro rata distribution rule, Section 4.3(i)'s requirement that returns of capital be pro rata, and Section 6.8(iii)'s unanimity requirement for distributions; clause (iii) also collides with Section 4.1(ii)'s permission to make additional contributions by consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences of pure mechanics; the only slip is citing "Regulation section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)" instead of the defined "Treasury Regulations."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.3(ii) distributes liquidation proceeds by Capital Account balances, giving this maintenance rule real consequences, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An advance is a debt "subject to such terms and conditions acceptable to the Company and each Member" — an agreement-to-agree that leaves the key terms undetermined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(v) requires unanimous Board approval for undertakings relating to indebtedness, which overlaps this member-consent mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It grants Members power over "any and all other rights or powers of the Company" not required to be done by the Board, then ends with "Except as provided herein, individually, the Members shall have no power to bind the Company" — a broad grant immediately qualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 makes the Board's management authority "Subject to Section 5.1," so each provision is made subordinate to the other — a circularity over who ultimately controls the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All ordinary and necessary out-of-pocket expenses incurred ... on behalf of the Company" is a mandatory reimbursement with an elastic qualifier and no approval gate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(xiv) subjects incurrence of material obligations to unanimous Board approval, and the Net Cash Flow definition expressly deducts these reimbursements, so the pieces fit but the discretion is unpoliced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence waiver in settled terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2's statement that a Member has no interest in specific Company property.
